title: Audit an electroplating proposal
promptMarkdown: A hypothetical Cu²⁺ plating process passes 0.800 A for 40.0 min at Faradaic efficiency 0.900. Use M(Cu)=63.546 g mol⁻¹. (a) Find charge, moles of electrons and copper deposited. (b) Its supply remains at 2.50 V. Find electrical input energy and explain why this is not the reversible chemical work from an unrelated standard cell voltage. (c) A manager doubles both time and current and predicts four times the mass and unchanged energy per gram. State the conditions under which that scaling holds and two reasons it can fail. (d) Specify a mass/charge/control measurement that would test the efficiency claim.
hintLadder: Convert minutes to seconds and separate electron moles from copper moles.
Efficiency applies to the fraction of charge used for Cu²⁺ reduction.
List the assumptions hidden in a linear scale-up.
